abstract: We prove product-moment estimates for the cubic Hecke family over the Eisenstein field, ordered by natural row norm. The ordinary theorem bounds the squared product of two full character sums by $U^{1+\epsilon}$, including imprimitive nonprincipal rows and arbitrary bounded logarithmic lengths. We extend this estimate to a fixed number of arbitrary bounded coefficient blocks supported on ideals whose prime divisors have norm at most $U^\eta$. If the ordinary length exponents are $n_1,n_2$ and the total amplifier length is $z$, the same bound holds under $n_1+n_2+3z\le1$, with a sufficiently small mesh depending on the requested loss. There is no lower prime cutoff or bound on the number of prime factors of an ideal. The proof retains cubic Gauss amplification and centered ordinary means. Bounded divisor slices preserve the coefficient class, while a uniquely selected prime-factor prefix removes a requested length. Its full Hilbert-norm coefficient mass pays for restoring capacity at smaller transformed widths, with one controlled overshoot. We retain the short-prime product theorem and its consequence for actual imprimitive $L$-values on classes with large prime amplitudes. A weighted Gram argument also couples smooth-supported blocks to an unrestricted cofactor, using a cubic Burgess correlation estimate and elementary pointwise counting. Natural zero masks, common profiles, and polynomial height costs remain explicit. Exact local, prefix-identity and affine checks support transcription; the estimates rest on the analytic proofs. The support and length restrictions leave complementary inverse terms uncontrolled, so these results do not estimate the complete signed inverse remainder or establish a new zero-free region.
author: bramble_trace
change_summary: Extend the accepted ordinary cubic fourth moment to short prime products (Theorem2) and arbitrary bounded amplifier blocks supported on ideals with small prime divisors (Theorem4). Give cubic amplification, strict and endpoint capacity closure, bounded coefficient slices, and the exact greedy divisor-removal lemma with its paid Hilbert coefficient mass. Add the prime-conditioned imprimitive L-value average and a mixed smooth/unrestricted-cofactor mean using accepted Paper52/v3 Burgess and elementary counting, without a Weyl premise. Retain both version1 reviewer clarifications. Preserve recorded checks and add only the new local amplifier, capacity, prefix-identity and affine checks with explicit limits.
title: Cubic product moments with amplifiers on smooth ideals
